biggest_catch: Students must find and book you — income depends entirely on winning students in a competitive teacher directory.
catches: Teachers are screened and vetted — application and approval required, not instant.
Platform commission applies on lesson fees (check the current schedule at signup).
Income depends on student bookings; new teachers start with zero students.
Free trial lessons and discounts are common ways to win first students — unpaid effort.

c1.evidence: Lessonface's official site describes the teacher channel: 'Teachers on Lessonface set their own rates and profiles, and students can select their ideal teachers based on their background, teaching style, rates, and schedule' — a real, public teacher deal channel operating since 2012.

c2.evidence: Official pages publish no fixed teacher pay range — teachers set their own rates (listings show e.g. $15–$50 per 30 minutes); framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: apply, get vetted, set rates and profile, get booked, teach via Zoom, get paid through Lessonface.

c4.evidence: Official FAQ: 'Registering an account is free' — no upfront fee to join as a teacher.

eligibility: Teachers in 300+ music, language, and arts subjects who can pass Lessonface's screening.
notes: Scenario: teaching (music/language/arts). Lessonface is a lesson marketplace: vetted teachers set their own rates and profiles, students browse and book, and lessons run over Zoom with payment handled by the platform. Income is per-lesson and variable — never guaranteed.
numeric_basis: payout: per-lesson teacher-set rates, no official fixed range. time: application + vetting + profile/rate setup, est. 45-90 min active.
payout_quote: Teachers on Lessonface set their own rates and profiles
payout_value_note: Teachers set their own per-lesson rates (listings show e.g. $15–$50 per 30 minutes); Lessonface publishes no fixed pay range — variable.

s1.note: Eligibility: teachers able to pass Lessonface's screening in a supported subject.

s2.note: Framed as teacher-set variable rates; no fixed amount promised.

s3.note: Catches cover vetting, commission, booking competition, and unpaid trial effort.

s4.note: Deduped: Lessonface absent from qa/existing-providers.txt, dedupe-check.py, and qa/verification/*.json (Wyzant/Preply/Superprof are separate catalog routes).

s6.note: Timing: bookings are continuous once approved; lessons scheduled per teacher availability.

s7.note: No weasel words in the mechanism description.

steps: Apply as a teacher on Lessonface and pass the screening/vetting for your subject.
Set your own rates, profile, and availability (group classes and courses optional).
Students browse profiles and book lessons with you.
Teach over Lessonface's secure Zoom links; get paid through the platform (commission applies).
timing: Bookings are continuous once approved; lessons are scheduled per your availability.
